mission: Reduce unnecessary process and state coupling without treating serverless as an ideological target. Preserve working domain behavior until a bounded migration seam is proven.

decisionPolicy.target: Prove the current production-shaped baseline, then migrate one evidence-backed seam at a time. KEEP is a valid final decision.
decisionPolicy.migrationAuthorizationRule: A stateful surface may not be changed by a serverless/stateless migration sprint unless its decisionStatus is approved, its evidence and validators are current, and the sprint owns only one named migrationSeam. Provisional entries fail closed to KEEP.
decisionPolicy.proofRule: Static or build proof may not be promoted to launcher/browser, behavior-observed, or live-runtime proof. Each migration sprint must report the strongest proof actually attained and its ceiling.

surfaces.name: Express request/runtime process
surfaces.currentResponsibility: Owns the production Node process, HTTP lifecycle, middleware/server startup, and application runtime boundary.
surfaces.stateHeld: Process-local runtime state plus access to external application state; exact per-request/process affinity must be proven before decomposition.
surfaces.stateLifetime: process and request scoped; exact long-lived state requires code evidence
surfaces.persistenceMechanism: primarily external PostgreSQL plus process memory; no serverless assumption is authorized by this ledger
surfaces.deploymentCoupling: Render starts the Node production launcher from the repository deployment contract.
invariants: Existing HTTP/API semantics remain stable.
/health remains DB-free liveness and /ready remains explicit DB readiness.
Production startup safety gates remain fail-closed.
evidence: .ai/codebase-map.json identifies server/index.ts as the Express process entry and render.yaml as the deployment blueprint.
Current deploy contracts and local production certification are the baseline proof surfaces.
surfaces.rationale: Do not remove the server before proving which responsibilities require process affinity and which can be stateless.
surfaces.migrationSeam: Factor one request/runtime responsibility at a time behind unchanged API/domain contracts.
prerequisites: Route/middleware ownership and process-affinity evidence are recorded.
forbiddenChanges: No wholesale server removal.
No API redesign bundled with runtime factoring.
No provider selection used as a substitute for architecture evidence.

surfaces.name: PostgreSQL / Drizzle domain persistence
surfaces.currentResponsibility: Stores durable application/domain state and owns schema evolution and recovery contracts.
surfaces.stateHeld: durable relational product state, account state, audit/event state, and migration ledger state
surfaces.persistenceMechanism: PostgreSQL accessed through Drizzle and repository database tooling
surfaces.deploymentCoupling: Production startup and recovery gates depend on database readiness, migrations, capacity policy, and backup evidence.
invariants: Domain persistence remains durable and transactionally correct.
Migration and recovery ledgers are not forged by migration work.
Backup/restore and evidence-preservation contracts remain valid.
evidence: .ai/codebase-map.json declares PostgreSQL/Drizzle as the current database shape.
.ai/ownership-rules.json assigns schema, migrations, and scripts/db to database-ops.
surfaces.rationale: A database incident is not evidence that relational persistence is unnecessary; storage/provider concerns must be separated from domain-state requirements.
surfaces.migrationSeam: Only factor a specific persistence adapter or data class after durability, transaction, cost, and recovery requirements are explicit.
prerequisites: The target data class and consistency model are documented.
Provider portability is evaluated separately from persistence semantics.
forbiddenChanges: No schema rewrite to satisfy a serverless slogan.
No destructive cleanup as architecture migration.
No moving domain invariants into prompts.

surfaces.name: Authentication and session state
surfaces.currentResponsibility: Protects identity, authentication, authorization, and session continuity.
surfaces.stateHeld: session/authentication state and security-sensitive identity context; exact stores and affinity require direct code inspection
surfaces.stateLifetime: request, session, and durable security-record lifetimes
surfaces.persistenceMechanism: unknown until the auth/session implementation and configuration are inspected
surfaces.deploymentCoupling: Environment secrets and production identity configuration participate in startup/readiness.
invariants: Authentication semantics and security posture cannot change implicitly.
Session continuity, revocation, CSRF/cookie behavior, and authorization must be preserved.
Secrets never enter tracked harness artifacts.
evidence: .ai/ownership-rules.json marks server/auth/** as security-owned high-risk scope.
Direct store/process-affinity evidence is still required before any migration decision.
surfaces.rationale: Auth/session state is a high-risk boundary; default to preservation until storage and process-affinity are proven.
surfaces.migrationSeam: Separate session storage/process affinity from authentication semantics without changing the public security contract.
prerequisites: Inspect concrete session store and cookie/auth configuration.
Identify all session invalidation and step-up flows.
forbiddenChanges: No auth provider swap bundled with serverless work.
No weakened session or authorization semantics.
No secrets in migration artifacts.

surfaces.name: Scheduled and background work
surfaces.currentResponsibility: Runs recurring retention, reminders, rollups, snapshots, and other background work where configured.
surfaces.stateHeld: job progress, schedules, retry/idempotency state, and effects depend on each worker implementation
surfaces.persistenceMechanism: mixed; inspect each worker before changing execution model
surfaces.deploymentCoupling: Some jobs are deployment/provider scheduled while others may be process-started; exact ownership must be inventoried.
invariants: Jobs remain idempotent or explicitly single-run where required.
Disabled resource-control posture is not silently reversed.
Retries cannot duplicate user-visible or financial effects.
evidence: .ai/codebase-map.json identifies scripts as operator/deployment tooling and server as workers/services.
render.yaml is a current deployment configuration surface; each job still needs code-level evidence.
surfaces.rationale: Managed scheduling may be appropriate, but moving a job does not remove its state, retry, or idempotency semantics.
surfaces.migrationSeam: Move one proven job boundary at a time while preserving its idempotency, retry, and data contracts.
prerequisites: Inventory job entry point and schedule.
Identify execution-time and external dependency requirements.
forbiddenChanges: No bulk migration of all workers.
No enabling disabled jobs as part of architecture work.
No implicit retry semantic changes.

surfaces.name: Filesystem and generated artifacts
surfaces.currentResponsibility: Produces build outputs, backups/evidence, generated agent artifacts, and operator reports under explicit tracking policies.
surfaces.stateHeld: generated files, evidence bundles, build output, and operator artifacts
surfaces.stateLifetime: ephemeral, release-durable, or protected external evidence depending on artifact class
surfaces.persistenceMechanism: repository-tracked docs for sanitized durable evidence; ignored local paths or protected external storage for runtime/private artifacts
surfaces.deploymentCoupling: Build output and some operator workflows depend on filesystem availability; production assumptions must be identified before function-style deployment.
invariants: Secrets, raw logs, dumps, user exports, and machine-local evidence remain untracked.
Tracked artifacts remain reproducible and sanitized.
Runtime evidence is not confused with source artifacts.
evidence: .ai/artifact-registry.json explicitly separates tracked release evidence from ignored .ai/runs/.ai/generated runtime artifacts.
The exact production-local filesystem dependence still requires path-level inspection.
surfaces.rationale: Filesystem use must be split by artifact class; some is build-time only and some may require external durable storage.
surfaces.migrationSeam: Externalize only one runtime-required artifact class after proving it cannot remain build-time/local/operator-owned.
prerequisites: Separate build-time, test-time, operator, and live-runtime filesystem uses.
forbiddenChanges: No blanket replacement of filesystem use with object storage.
No tracking private runtime artifacts.
No changing backup/evidence confidentiality boundaries.

surfaces.name: Deployment and production startup orchestration
surfaces.currentResponsibility: Builds, gates, starts, certifies, and reports the production-shaped application.
surfaces.stateHeld: deployment configuration, candidate identity, gate results, and runtime proof
surfaces.stateLifetime: per candidate/deployment plus durable release evidence
surfaces.persistenceMechanism: tracked configuration plus CI/runtime evidence artifacts
surfaces.deploymentCoupling: Currently Render-oriented with repository-owned production startup and local-cert contracts.
invariants: Repository/CI proof never masquerades as live proof.
Production mutation requires explicit authorization.
Current startup, health, migration, and capacity safety gates stay intact until replacements are proven.
evidence: .ai/codebase-map.json records Render as current provider and no direct live deploy command as registered.
Current harness has predeploy and local production certification workflows.
surfaces.rationale: Deployment provider changes are downstream of application/state factoring, not evidence for it.
surfaces.migrationSeam: Replace one deployment adapter only after the application runtime contract is provider-neutral and equivalently certified.
prerequisites: Current baseline candidate passes local production certification.
Required runtime capabilities for the target deployment class are explicit.
forbiddenChanges: No provider-first rewrite.
No weakening health/readiness or startup gates.
No live provider mutation without operator authorization.

surfaces.name: Cache and queue dependencies
surfaces.currentResponsibility: Potential caching/queue/runtime coordination surface; concrete production use must be proven by code search before architectural treatment.
surfaces.stateHeld: unknown until concrete clients, keys, queues, and consumers are enumerated
consumers: unknown until repository evidence identifies active usage
surfaces.deploymentCoupling: Unknown until active imports/configuration and production requirements are proven.
invariants: Do not introduce a queue/cache merely to make the architecture look serverless.
Do not remove an active coordination mechanism without proving consumers and failure semantics.
evidence: Dependency declarations alone do not prove active runtime use; direct import/configuration evidence is required.
surfaces.rationale: Fail closed until repository evidence proves whether caches/queues are active, obsolete, or unnecessary.
surfaces.migrationSeam: First classify active versus unused dependencies; only then assign a bounded queue/cache migration seam.
prerequisites: Identify producers, consumers, retry semantics, and persistence expectations.
forbiddenChanges: No new queue/cache service before evidence.
No dependency deletion based only on package.json presence or absence.

surfaces.name: Harness / routing / application integration seams
surfaces.currentResponsibility: Keeps agent orchestration, executable capabilities, and application/domain implementation separate and explicitly connected.
surfaces.stateHeld: run context, validation plans, artifacts, workflow state, and product state in their respective systems
surfaces.stateLifetime: per run plus durable tracked contracts
surfaces.persistenceMechanism: tracked harness contracts plus application-owned state stores
surfaces.deploymentCoupling: Harness may orchestrate deployment work but must never become the only implementation of product behavior.
invariants: Skills describe reusable workflow guidance.
Capabilities expose reusable operations.
Triggers deterministically route conditions.
Application logic remains in code/domain contracts, not hidden in prompts.
evidence: The existing harness already separates workflows, skills, capabilities, triggers, validators, artifacts, and ownership rules.
surfaces.rationale: This separation is the guardrail that prevents architecture migration from becoming prompt-only behavior.
surfaces.migrationSeam: No migration; preserve the integration boundary and extend it only with deterministic executable contracts.
forbiddenChanges: No product behavior implemented only in prompts.
No trigger conditions that rely on agent intuition when deterministic evidence exists.
No capability claiming execution it cannot perform.
